concepts.title: Physical Properties of Metals and Non-metals

questions.q: State two physical properties each of metals and non-metals.
questions.a: Metals: lustrous, good conductors, sonorous, malleable. Non-metals: dull, poor conductors, brittle.

questions.q: Name a non-metal that conducts electricity and a metal that is liquid at room temperature.
questions.a: Graphite conducts; mercury is the liquid metal.

questions.q: Why can metals be drawn into wires?
questions.a: Metals are ductile - their layers of atoms can slide without breaking the metallic bond.

questions.q: What happens when iron reacts with steam?
questions.a: Iron oxide (Fe3O4) and hydrogen gas form - iron does not react with cold or hot water, only steam.

questions.q: Why is sodium stored in kerosene?
questions.a: Sodium reacts so fast with air and moisture that it catches fire; kerosene keeps air away.

questions.q: What is an amphoteric oxide? Give an example.
questions.a: An oxide reacting with both acids and bases, e.g. aluminium oxide or zinc oxide.

questions.q: Arrange the steps of extracting a metal from its sulphide ore.
questions.a: Concentration of ore, roasting in air to oxide, then reduction of the oxide to metal (and refining).

questions.q: Why is aluminium used to reduce metal oxides like manganese dioxide?
questions.a: Aluminium is highly reactive and its reaction with oxides releases great heat (thermite), reducing them to metal.
